> Somsack is born in Taifafeki, grows up in Onesa, and one year later a Taifafeki
> doctor can see every vaccine he has ever had, without a single record being
> copied across the border.

The story is the one the [journeys walkthrough](en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/overview/) tells, moment by
moment, with the people, the technical layer and the policy questions
(interactive; its source is `web/` in this repository),
documented here as a WHO SMART Guidelines L2 DAK and L3 implementation guide.
Its FHIR examples are materialized in this guide; the
[Journey examples](vaxlink-examples.html) page maps each moment and device screen
to them.

- **Country A** (birth country) is **Taifafeki**. Somsack is born at Kesaro
  Provincial Hospital and gets his birth doses there (J1). On the GDHCN DEV
  network, Taifafeki is played by the test participant **XXR**, whose DSC (kid
  `kW/6VnwPRKI=`, hex `916ffa567c0f44a2`) is on the live DEV trust list.
- **Country B** (country of residence, "home") is **Onesa**. The family
  lives there (J2, J3, J4.0). On the DEV network it is played by a fictional
  participant, written **XXK**.
- J4.1 takes the family back to Taifafeki, a year later.

XXR and XXK are DEV test participants, not either country's production keys,
and nothing here implies a real ministry. Every person is fictional.

**The cast:** Khamla SENGMANY (mother), Bounmy SENGMANY (father, holds the
family phone), Vilay (community health worker, Village 04), Nurse
Chanthasone (Lomaru District Health Center) and Dr Anan (Taifafeki
clinician, at the birth and a year later).

#### J1 — Born abroad (Taifafeki, birth day)

**Precondition: the issuer's DSC is on the trust list.** XXR's document signer certificate (DSC), issued under XXR's Country Signing CA (CSCA), was shared with the GDHCN, the Trust Anchor, before any DVC is signed; the GDHCN publishes it as a DID document. Sharing it is not a step of issuing. A DVC signed with a key whose DSC was never shared fails every receiver's trust-list check ([STT-VER-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-006)).

Khamla gives birth to Somsack on 2025-10-28 at Kesaro Provincial
Hospital, away from home. He has no Taifafeki identity number. Dr Anan gives the
Hep B and BCG birth doses and records them with their WHO PreQual product
codes. For each dose, the hospital system does three things:

1. It builds a DVCMinPreQual payload: [STT-PAY-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-pay-001)…[005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-pay-005) and [STT-PAY-007](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-pay-007), with subclaim −6 ([STT-SEL-003](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-sel-003)). No identity document is needed ([STT-PAY-005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-pay-005)).
2. It prepares the CWT and the bytes to sign: [STT-CWT-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cwt-001)…[005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cwt-005), [STT-ISS-004](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-iss-004).
3. It has XXR's key sign them ([STT-COS-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cos-002), [STT-COS-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cos-006)), then finishes the HC1 text: [STT-COS-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cos-001), [STT-ZIP-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-zip-001), [STT-B45-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-b45-001), [STT-HC1-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-hc1-001), [STT-QR-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-qr-001).

Khamla leaves with two paper DVCs.
*In the demo:* the library tests use the WHO guide's own two signed HC1
strings ([QR Code Generation §12](https://smart.who.int/trust/qr_code_generation.html)),
which verify against the live DEV trust list under the same XXR key. Somsack's
DVC payloads are illustrative. Live issuance in the app uses a
TEST-ONLY key ([STT-ISS-003](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-iss-003)), whose DSC is not on the GDHCN list, so its DVCs
do not verify in J3.

- *Pain point:* The baby has no Taifafeki ID number, so his records would normally stay locked inside the Taifafeki hospital’s system.
- *Enabler:* A digitally signed QR card travels with the family — no ID number or database lookup needed.
- *Policy:* Babies born abroad can get a verifiable vaccine record before they have the host country’s civil registration or a national ID — and registering the birth at home still matters.

#### J2 — Found at home (Onesa, 3 weeks later)

**J2a.** On a routine visit to Village 04, Vilay finds a newborn the Onesan
system does not know exists. Her phone has had no signal for weeks. Khamla
shows the two cards. The CHW app reads them with **read-unverified**
([STT-VER-011](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-011); [STT-B45-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-b45-002), [STT-ZIP-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-zip-002), [STT-CBR-003](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cbr-003)), which needs no trust
list. It shows the doses, but checks no signature and saves nothing yet.

**J2b.** On the CHW app's newborn form (structured data capture,
`TrustDemoHouseholdRegistration`) she adds Somsack to the Sengmany household
(`TrustDemoHousehold`), with a temporary id. Bounmy confirms the details as
head of household. The app saves the doses read from the cards as reported by
the family, not verified (`TrustDemoJ2HepBReported`, `TrustDemoJ2BcgReported`:
`primarySource` false). Vilay refers Somsack to the district health center
(`TrustDemoJ2Referral`). Everything stays queued on the phone, for 28 days if
need be, and syncs when it next reaches a signal.

- *Pain point (J2a):* Without a check, a forged or mistyped card could quietly become an official record.
- *Pain point (J2b):* Babies born abroad are invisible to the home health system until civil registration catches up — sometimes months later.
- *Enabler (J2a):* The phone reads the card offline, and keeps “what the family told us” clearly separate from “what we have verified”.
- *Enabler (J2b):* An offline form links the baby to his household immediately; it syncs once the phone finds a signal.
- *Policy (J2a):* Keep a clear line between what families report and what has been verified, and don’t grant trust too early.
- *Policy (J2b):* Newborns can be registered at home, offline, before civil registration or a national ID exists.

#### J3 — Made official (Lomaru District Health Center, 4 weeks later)

**Precondition: the DID documents are already loaded.** Loading them is not a step of this visit. The clinic may be offline all day, so the EHR fetches nothing during it: its trust store holds the GDHCN DEV trust list as it was last refreshed, including XXR's DSC DID document ([STT-TRU-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-001), [STT-TRU-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-002), [STT-TRU-005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-005)). A clinic with no connection of its own refreshes it about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office, where Country B retrieves the list the GDHCN trust anchor distributes. A DSC published after that refresh is not in the clinic's copy, so its DVC fails the trust-list check ([STT-VER-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-006)) until the next refresh.

**J3a.** Nurse Chanthasone opens the referral and scans the QRs. The EHR
**verifies** each DVC offline against that copy ([STT-VER-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-001)…[009](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-009),
[STT-KID-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-kid-002)), without contacting Taifafeki. Both verify, so it imports them as
FHIR `Immunization`s (`TrustDemoJ3HepB`, `TrustDemoJ3Bcg`) with provenance
(`TrustDemoJ3Verification`; [STT-VER-007](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-007), [STT-VER-008](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-008)), replacing the reported
doses of J2. If a DVC fails (a tampered card, say), the EHR names the step and
the reason, the doses stay unverified, and the nurse decides by national
catch-up policy.

**J3b.** The Taifafeki Hep B product matches nothing on the national schedule.
The EHR keeps Taifafeki's product coding and adds the schedule coding beside
it, from the national map (`TrustDemoProductToOnesaEpi`). For the Hep B product
the map has no entry, so Nurse Chanthasone makes the clinical call that it is
the schedule's birth dose (`TrustDemoJ3Adjudication`), and her decision is
added to the map for the next clinic. The schedule (`TrustDemoOnesaInfantSchedule`)
then runs: the birth doses count, and pentavalent 1, bOPV 1 and PCV 1 are due
at 6 weeks (`TrustDemoJ3Recommendation`). Khamla leaves with the date
(`TrustDemoJ3Reminder`). Over the year Somsack gets those doses and
measles-rubella at 9 months, in Onesa.

- *Pain point (J3a):* Clinicians either distrust foreign paper and re-vaccinate, or trust it blindly.
- *Pain point (J3b):* Countries name and package vaccines differently, so doses get missed or repeated.
- *Enabler (J3a):* Taifafeki’s signing key is on the shared WHO trust list, so any clinic can check it locally.
- *Enabler (J3b):* Taifafeki’s original code is kept and the Onesan code is added alongside; the schedule engine calculates what’s due.
- *Policy (J3a):* Trust is decentralized: an Onesan clinic verifies a Taifafeki signature itself, without contacting Taifafeki.
- *Policy (J3b):* Never overwrite another country’s record: keep the original coding alongside the national one.

#### J4.0 — Crossing back: one family, one phone (Onesa, 12 months later)

**J4.0a.** The family plans a trip to Taifafeki. Bounmy's phone holds the
family wallet, with a profile for each of them. Somsack's summary
(`TrustDemoJ4Ips`) shows six doses: two from Taifafeki, four from Onesa.

**Precondition, as in J1:** Country B's DSC, under Country B's CSCA, is already shared with the GDHCN, the Trust Anchor. That is what lets the clinic in Taifafeki verify the link in J4.1.

**J4.0b.** For Somsack, Bounmy shares his record with a 4-digit passcode he
can say aloud, valid for 14 days. The portal records his consent
(`TrustDemoJ4Consent`), then does three things:

1. It assembles the IPS and Somsack's DVCs.
2. It encrypts them ([STT-VHL-004](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-004), [STT-VHL-007](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-007)) behind a passcode-protected manifest with an expiry ([STT-VHL-009](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-009)).
3. It issues the link as an HCERT, with the VHL at key 5 ([STT-VHL-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-001), [STT-VHL-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-002)), signed with Country B's DSC.

The QR holds only a pointer and a key: the record stays in Onesa.

- *Pain point (J4.0a):* Many families share one smartphone; one-app-per-person designs leave them out.
- *Pain point (J4.0b):* Sending photos or PDFs of records leaks data and can’t be verified by the receiver.
- *Enabler (J4.0a):* A household wallet on one phone, with a separate health summary for each person.
- *Enabler (J4.0b):* A Verifiable Health Link: the QR holds only a locked pointer; the data stays home until the passcode is given.
- *Policy (J4.0a):* Design for shared devices (“One Family, One Phone”) so families with only one phone aren’t left out.
- *Policy (J4.0b):* Data sovereignty: the record stays in Onesa until the family authorizes someone to open it.

#### J4.1 — Crossing back: a Taifafeki doctor sees the full history (Kesaro, 12 months later)

**Precondition, as in J3: the DID documents are already loaded.** The clinic viewer's trust store is a cached copy of the GDHCN trust list, including Country B's DSC DID document ([STT-TRU-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-001), [STT-TRU-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-002), [STT-TRU-005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-005)). The clinic refreshes it nightly or hourly, against about weekly at the offline J3 clinic. It does not need to be online to verify: verifying reads the cache and never fetches the list. A DSC published after the last refresh fails the trust-list check ([STT-VER-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-006)), naming that reason.

Back where it began, Dr Anan sees Somsack at a primary care clinic in
Kesaro. Bounmy shows the QR on his phone and says the passcode. The
clinic viewer and the Onesan gateway take five steps:

1. The viewer verifies the HCERT against Country B's DSC in its copy of the trust list.
2. It requests the manifest by ITI-YY5, signed with HTTP Message Signatures ([STT-VHL-005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-005), [STT-VHL-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-006), [STT-VHL-008](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-008)).
3. The Onesan gateway checks the passcode, the expiry and the consent, returns the manifest, and logs the access at home (`TrustDemoJ41Access`).
4. The viewer decrypts the IPS and DVCs ([STT-VHL-007](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-007)) (`TrustDemoJ41Received`).
5. It shows them to Dr Anan: every dose since the birth, viewed, never copied.

A wrong passcode is refused, and the attempt is still logged in Onesa
(`TrustDemoJ41WrongPasscode`). If the HCERT does not verify (for example,
Country B's DSC is missing from the cached list), there is no digital
verification. The clinic names the step and the reason ([STT-VER-008](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-008)), does not
follow the VHL, and Dr Anan treats whatever the family can show as he
would a paper record.

- *Pain point:* Without the history, the doctor would repeat vaccines or have to guess.
- *Enabler:* The record is fetched live from Onesa, viewed without being copied, and an access log is sent home.
- *Policy:* Continuity of care across borders: each country keeps its own records, with no international patient registry and no vendor lock-in. What is agreed regionally is the data model and the trust list, not a shared copy of the data.

### Questions for discussion

The journeys walkthrough closes with four policy questions:

1. **Identity for babies born abroad** (J1, J2b): how should national immunization systems handle temporary ids for cross-border infants before civil registration is complete?
2. **Where trust begins** (J2a, J3a): why should offline CHW devices store foreign cards as reported, not verified, rather than verify them in the field?
3. **Matching vaccines across countries** (J3b): when a monovalent vaccine is given abroad but the home schedule uses a combination (pentavalent), how should schedule rules count the doses still due?
4. **Cross-border access and audit** (J4.0b, J4.1): what agreements do countries need so that a clinician viewing a record abroad triggers an audit entry in the patient's home country?
